description: HOT publishes regularly refreshed OpenStreetMap extracts for each country on the Humanitarian Data Exchange, one dataset per country and theme. They are produced by the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's raw-data export service from OpenStreetMap contributors' data, to give humanitarian responders ready-to-use layers. On 2026-09-26 the HDX search API listed, by dataset name, 251 buildings, 249 health-facility, 248 education-facility, 249 roads, 249 waterways, 249 points-of-interest, 249 populated-places, 248 financial-services, 246 railways, 249 airports and 247 sea-ports datasets, plus a few sub-national extracts such as Mokwa Town in Nigeria and Goma. The Algeria buildings dataset selects every feature with a building tag and keeps name, building type, levels, material, address and other tags as attributes; it was modified on 9 August 2026. The Ghana sea-ports dataset selects port, harbour and ferry-terminal features and was modified on 10 September 2026. Coverage: every country, with depth depending on where volunteers have mapped. Access: Shapefile, KML, GeoJSON and GeoPackage files hosted on HOT's cloud storage, with the CKAN API for automated discovery; the HOT Export Tool makes custom extracts. Licence: Open Database License (ODbL), attribution to OpenStreetMap contributors; free. Caveats: HDX notes that crowd-sourced OpenStreetMap data cannot be considered exhaustive; urban areas are usually better mapped than remote ones, and attributes such as levels vary widely. Simulation uses are building and facility exposure layers for hazard and humanitarian scenarios, accessibility to health and education facilities, port and airport logistics, and emergency response planning. Related records: HOT disaster-response datasets on HDX, Overture Maps buildings and Healthsites.io.
